vignette: A young child who is poorly cooperative has a cervical carious lesion on the facial surface of a primary maxillary incisor. The clinician plans a composite restoration.
stem: Which statement is most consistent with the available guidance for restoring this tooth?

options.text: The preparation should follow a design fundamentally different from the one used on permanent teeth.
The preparation can follow the same general form used for a Class V lesion on a permanent tooth.
Composite can be placed in any young child, because adequate isolation can always be achieved regardless of cooperation.
Techniques for restoring primary anterior teeth rest mainly on high-level controlled trial evidence rather than expert opinion.
